slides.title: Member Function Ref-Qualifiers (& and &&)
slides.prompt: Ref-qualifiers allow member functions to be overloaded based on whether the object (*this) is an lvalue or an rvalue. This enables move-aware API design where temporaries can return internal data via move instead of copy.

slides.title: Lvalue Ref-Qualifier Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the qualifier token applied after member method parameter list to restrict execution to lvalue objects.

slides.title: Rvalue Ref-Qualified Method Invocation
slides.prompt: When is a member method qualified with '&&' invoked?
options: When the method is called on temporary rvalue instances or objects cast via std::move(*this)
When the function receives rvalue parameters
Only when static memory allocation is used
When called concurrently from multiple threads
slides.correctAnswer: When the method is called on temporary rvalue instances or objects cast via std::move(*this)

slides.title: Ref-Qualifier Overloading Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the qualifier for stealing internal state when chaining methods on temporary rvalues.

slides.title: Preventing Assignment to Temporaries
slides.prompt: How can ref-qualifiers prevent accidental code like 'Foo() = bar();' where an assignment is attempted on a temporary instance?
options: Qualify operator= with lvalue ref-qualifier '&' so assignment is permitted only on lvalue objects
slides.correctAnswer: Qualify operator= with lvalue ref-qualifier '&' so assignment is permitted only on lvalue objects

slides.title: Lvalue Ref-Qualified Assignment Operator
slides.prompt: Fill in the ref-qualifier to restrict copy assignment to lvalues.

slides.title: Mixing Qualified and Unqualified Overloads
slides.prompt: Can you declare both a ref-qualified overload (e.g. void f() &;) and an unqualified overload (void f();) inside the same class?
options: No, if any overload of a member function has a ref-qualifier, all overloads of that function must have ref-qualifiers
Only if one of them is marked const
slides.correctAnswer: No, if any overload of a member function has a ref-qualifier, all overloads of that function must have ref-qualifiers

slides.title: Const Rvalue Ref-Qualifier Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the combined qualifier specifiers for const rvalue object instances.

slides.title: Move-Aware Method Chaining (Fluent Interfaces)
slides.prompt: Why are ref-qualifiers useful in Builder or Fluent API patterns?
options: They allow move operations on temporary builder chains without copying intermediate configurations
They replace the need for virtual destructors
They force synchronous execution on GPU buffers
They automatically lock thread mutexes during builder steps
slides.correctAnswer: They allow move operations on temporary builder chains without copying intermediate configurations
